Final for Publication

NARRATIVE & PLANS
FOR TYPE 1 ZONING MAP AMENDMENT
AT 2658 W 215T PLACE, CHICAGO, IL 60608
FROM RT-4 TO RM-6

The petitioner is proposing to renovate an existing three dwelling unit multi-family
residential building located at 2658 W. 21% Place on the northeast corner of 21 Place and
Washtenaw Avenue. The proposed renovation will include an increase from three dwelling units
to eight dwelling units. The petitioner is requesting approval of a rezoning from RT-4 to RM-6 to
accommodate the increase in floor area ratio to 4.40; an administrative adjustment under section
17-13-1003-EE as the building is located in a Transit-Serviced Location.

Specifically, the renovation of the building will consist of remodeling the ground floor
from one inefficiently large dwelling unit and tenant storage to three dwelling units; remodeling
the basement level from unused mechanical and storage spaces to three dwelling units; and
maintaining the two dwelling units on the second floor. A specific floor plan of the proposed
layout is enclosed with this application. The existing structure will also be repaired and/or
replaced as necessary. The existing mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems will be
modified and updated to accommodate for the new layout. New electrical and water services will
be provided. In addition, the exterior envelope will be renovated to provide a weather-tight
enclosure. The work shall include, but not be limited to, repair and/or replace and tuckpoint the
existing masonry as necessary. The plans provide new windows and doors as required and
provide roof repair and/or replacement as necessary. The plans do not propose to significantly
alter the external condition of the property beyond the aesthetic refreshment of the existing
structure. No addition is proposed, and the proposed plans will not change the massing of the
building or alter the current height of the structure, which is 26 feet. All work shall be within the
existing exterior walls.

The building is an existing nonconforming development, under 17-15-0400, as it was
lawfully constructed in its current layout in 1902, prior to the standards of the current Zoning
Ordinance. The building’s nonconformities include it nonconformity with the following
standards: setbacks, off-street parking and rear-yard open-area standards. As there is no work
being performed that would increase the extent of the building’s nonconformity, no relief is
needed for these nonconformities.

In addition to the building’s lawful nonconforming development under 17-15-0400, an
administrative adjustment under sections 17-12-1003-EE(1) and 17-10-0102-B(1) is sought to
reduce the minimum off-street automobile parking requirement by 100 percent. The property
itself has no space to include parking, as the existing building takes up the entire lot. The
building is located within a Transit-Serviced Location, as it is located within 2,640 feet of the
CTA Pink Line station at 2011 S. California Ave and within 1,320 feet of multiple CTA bus line

The proposed renovation will significantly improve the community’s appreciation of the
property by providing a much needed aesthetic beautification that will increase visual appeal in
the neighborhood. The property as currently extant was purchased by the owner as an abandoned
building. In addition, it will increase housing access and density in a neighborhood that needs
smaller and more affordable units; as the proposed interior renovations provides for eight two-
bedroom apartments to replace the three large and less affordable units currently present.
